title.en: Expressing needs and wishes: precisar and querer

summary.en: Precisar and querer attach directly to a following verb, while precisar takes de before a noun.

body.en:
From season 1, episodes 1 and 2.

Searching for his reading glasses, Seu Otavio says *Eu preciso ler o caderno de reservas*, Dona Helena smiles *É tudo o que eu quero*, and in the kitchen Bianca protests *Meu pão doce precisa de manteiga sem sal!*

Before another action, both *precisar* ('to need') and *querer* ('to want') link straight to the infinitive with no extra preposition: *eu preciso saber* ('I need to know'), *preciso comprar* ('I need to buy'), *quero ver* ('I want to see').

Watch the one small switch when a noun follows *precisar*: Portuguese inserts *de* ('of') before the thing needed—*precisa de manteiga* ('needs butter')—whereas *querer* takes a noun directly (*quero um café*).
